acceptance: Receiver refund and settlement observations preserve unique block/log identity, durable historical coverage and finalized independent-provider evidence.

Complete preceding records support balanced idempotent refunds held-first/payable-second and settlements payable-first/held-second; policy exceptions and unreconciled observations stay explicit without invented or negative balances.

Real-contract tests cover repeated/partial returns, paid-unsettled refunds, catch-up, multiple logs, reorgs, external settlement, native mismatch and refund-to-wallet attribution; independent balances and ledger equations reconcile.

tasks.behavior: Add merchant payment operations and store reconciliation APIs
acceptance: Payments include all permitted attempts with stable paging and source/store/status filters; detail separates deposits, settlement, refunds, reconciliation and delivery state.
Attention identifies partial/held/uncertain payments, delayed/refused settlements and failed/disabled delivery with evidence-backed reasons and valid next actions.
Exact movement CSV rows preserve store, source, invoice/order reference, chain/token/decimals and transaction/log evidence, without repeating independently summable aggregate totals.

Tenant, assigned-store and key-mode tests pass; exports and canonical snapshot totals reconcile to ledger and independent finalized chain records, with verification coverage and unmatched observations explicit.

tasks.behavior: Give merchants distinct payments, links and invoice workflows
acceptance: Payments and Needs attention expose coherent store-filtered operational lists and detail; links show resulting payments with explicit Edit; invoices remain customer billing.
Overview, lists, detail, checkout, receipts and exports use matching payment/settlement/refund meanings and resource cross-links.
Failed store/token loading never silently chooses a default or restores invalid acceptance; customer invoice composition identifies its recipient.
Desktop and phone walkthroughs, accessibility and authorization checks pass while valid legacy invoice URLs remain usable.

tasks.behavior: Guide merchants through supported setup tasks
acceptance: Merchant and developer setup guides sharing a link, billing a customer or integrating checkout using actual billing/store/branding/acceptance/key/origin/webhook state.
The existing first store is reused; completion survives reload through actual resources and respects role permissions.
KYB honestly remains not_required and never blocks test keys or invoices; obsolete API-later messaging is removed.

tasks.behavior: Implement hosted and origin-restricted embedded checkout
acceptance: Hosted integration works without a browser package; full and element embeds reuse trusted checkout and support existing payment lifecycles.
Only configured exact origins can frame an embed; normal pay pages remain unframeable; loopback HTTP is test-only and live returns require HTTPS.
Message origin/source checks, strict CSP, revocation, expiration and forged parent/redirect events are tested; browser hints never prove fulfillment.

tasks.behavior: Build minimal JavaScript and React checkout packages
acceptance: Browser packages provide PayButton, Checkout and PaymentElement over existing checkout URLs, without secret keys or client-authoritative financial state.
Typed messages verify origin/source and mount lifecycle cleans listeners; React 18 and 19 compatibility, type/build/size and packed-install checks pass.
Release artifacts, changelogs and provenance CI are prepared; publishing remains gated by separate approval.

tasks.behavior: Prove merchant checkout fulfillment and reconciliation end to end
acceptance: The example merchant prices a cart on its server, creates real checkouts, verifies events and fulfills an order once across hosted and embedded flows.
Independent shared-link customers, client invoicing, multi-store isolation, expiration, partial payment, delivery recovery and spoofed prices/messages have automated workflow coverage.
Ledger/export totals reconcile against receiver and wallet chain balances; duplicate/reordered events cannot double-fulfill.
Quickstart and integration docs match implemented packages; provider limitations, actual user testing and release approvals are reported truthfully.
